svg.title: Completeness on real TOIs, against the published references in matched bins
svg.desc: Blind benchmark on 662 real TESS Objects of Interest (NASA Exoplanet Archive TOI table, fetched 2026-10-19, seed 20261019), held-out half, the three Probes. Completeness is the share of confirmed or known planets (CP/KP) on searchable stars recovered as a vetted dip on the ephemeris, with Wilson 95% intervals. Left, in the bins the published references use: All radii: SetuHQ 57% (86/150, 49%–65%) against Kepler Robovetter DR25 > 85% (vetting only, on detected TCEs, P < 100 d); 3–4 R⊕: SetuHQ 44% (4/9, 19%–73%) against Planet Hunters TESS 51% (a citizen-science search); > 4 R⊕: SetuHQ 75% (77/102, 66%–83%) against Planet Hunters TESS 85% (a citizen-science search). SetuHQ is below the Kepler Robovetter's completeness and Planet Hunters TESS's rate above 4 R⊕ (each interval excludes the reference); consistent with Planet Hunters TESS's rate at 3 to 4 R⊕ (9 stars: the interval includes it). Right: overall 57% (86/150, 49%–65%); without the stars exposed to the known clipping bug 53% (65/123). By planet radius: < 2 R⊕: 10% (2/20, 3%–30%); 2–4 R⊕: 23% (6/26, 11%–42%); 4–8 R⊕: 36% (4/11, 15%–65%); > 8 R⊕: 80% (73/91, 71%–87%). By period: 0.5–2 d: 41% (12/29, 26%–59%); 2–5 d: 67% (52/78, 56%–76%); 5–13 d: 51% (22/43, 37%–65%). References as stated in the report: Thompson et al. 2018; Eisner et al. 2021. Measured on a stated benchmark, not discoveries. Sources: docs/results/benchmark_real_tois.json, docs/results/benchmark_toi_sample.json (radii) and docs/results/benchmark_real_tois.md (references), commit 1180dfe.
